findings.issue_text: `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-16`
`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25`

`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` — `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Values come from a site setting an admin typed. A `'` in the value produces a syntax error and aborts the migration mid-flight; it is also a textbook injection sink. Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized `exec_insert`.
`app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3`

`obj[k].map(...)` assumes the value is an array. Any rest-serializer payload with a `*_ids` key that is `null` or a scalar throws `TypeError` and takes down the whole hydrate. Guard with `Ember.isArray`.
`hydrated || []` is dead code — `Array.prototype.map` always returns an array.

The branch does `delete obj[k]` **unconditionally**, unlike the singular branch which only deletes when hydration succeeded. Unresolvable ids are silently replaced by `undefined` entries *and* the raw ids are discarded, so callers can't recover. At minimum `.filter(x => x)` the result and keep `obj[k]` when nothing resolved.
`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10-16, 23`

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` for an unknown id; `update` then calls `host.host =` and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` → `NoMethodError` → 500. Use `find_by`/`find` and raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` 500s if the `embeddable_host` key is missing, and assigns `nil` if `host` is absent — which then hits issue #7. Use `params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(:host, :category_id)`.

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8` — `self.host.sub!` is a `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil, so a missing `host` produces a 500 rather than the intended `validates_format_of` error. Guard: `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`. Also prefer non-bang `sub` with reassignment — in-place mutation of an AR attribute string is fragile w.r.t. dirty tracking.

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17` — `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the *column* but not the *parameter*. A mixed-case host (e.g. a `feed_polling_url` or embed URL of `http://EvilTrout.com/...` flowing through `TopicRetriever` / `TopicEmbed.import`) will never match. Add `.downcase` to the argument, and ideally downcase `host` in `before_validation` so the stored value is canonical.

`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5` both only assert `Controller < Admin::AdminController`. These pass even if create/update/destroy are completely broken — and given issues #4, #6 and #7, they demonstrably do pass against broken code. There is **zero** coverage for: host normalization (`http://` and path stripping), `host_allowed?`, `record_for_host` returning the right category, the create/update/destroy round trip, the uncategorized fallback, or the migration's data backfill. This is the core of the feature. At minimum add a `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` and real request specs.

`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11` accepts `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` and returns 200 having saved nothing. On the client, `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:6-8` `saveChanges` calls `embedding.update({})` but **no template invokes `saveChanges`** — `embedding.hbs` has no save button. Either drop both (hosts are saved per-row by the component, so nothing else needs saving) or finish the intent. Shipping a route that silently pretends to save is worse than not having it.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11-15`** — `record_for_host` returns `false` on bad input but `nil` from `.first`. Inconsistent; return `nil` throughout. (`false.try(:category_id)` happens to be safe in Rails 4, so no live bug.)
**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2`** — regex anchored with `\Z`, which permits a trailing newline; use `\z`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` TLD rule also rejects `localhost` and newer long TLDs.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:3`** — `belongs_to :category` with a `null: false` column but no `validates_presence_of :category_id` and no FK. A nil/nonexistent `category_id` from a direct API call becomes a `StatementInvalid` 500 or a dangling reference.

**`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3`** and **`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:3`** — `ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` are already applied by `Admin::AdminController`, and the routes additionally carry `AdminConstraint`. Redundant.
**`config/routes.rb:153`** — `resources :embeddable_hosts` generates `index`/`show`/`new`/`edit` routes with no corresponding actions. Scope to `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`.

**`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3`** — `create_table ..., force: true` will silently drop a pre-existing table. Also the migration is written as `change` but contains irreversible `execute` statements, so `rake db:rollback` will fail. Use `up`/`down`.

**`app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14`** — all three method overrides (`id`, `host`, `category_id`) just return `object.<attr>`, which is exactly what `attributes` already does. Delete them.
**`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:16`** — `OpenStruct` without `require 'ostruct'`; relies on some other gem having required it. Also `.order(:host)` is a case-sensitive sort.

**`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22`** — `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the *first* underscore; a three-word admin model would silently miss the `/admin/` prefix. Use `/_/g`.

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:37-40`** — after a successful save the buffer is never committed (`commitBuffer()`), unlike sibling admin editors; a later cancel can roll back to a stale value. Also `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` may receive a string id from `category-chooser`.
**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs`** — inline `style='width: 50%'` rather than a stylesheet class; no `thead`/`tbody`; no empty-state message when there are no hosts.
**`config/locales/client.en.yml`** — the `admin.embedding.edit` key is added but never referenced.

**Backward compatibility** — removing `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`, `SiteSetting.embed_category`, and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` is a breaking change for any plugin referencing them, and the removed keys still exist in the non-English locale files. Worth a deprecation note in the release notes.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-16`

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the table is created with `force: true` (within lines 9-16). In Rails migrations this will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, which can cause unintended data loss if the migration is re-run (e.g., during a failed deploy/rollback or in non-production environments). This is a concrete, verifiable risk introduced by the diff and is generally considered a defect in migration safety.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25`

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the migration inserts rows via raw SQL with direct string interpolation: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Because `h` comes from the existing `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` value, any host containing a single quote (or other SQL-special characters) will break the SQL (migration failure) and, in principle, allows SQL injection within the migration context. There is no quoting/escaping (e.g., `connection.quote(h)`), and validations/callbacks are bypassed because it’s a direct `execute`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` — `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Values come from a site setting an admin typed. A `'` in the value produces a syntax error and aborts the migration mid-flight; it is also a textbook injection sink. Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized `exec_insert`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` row for `embeddable_hosts` (admin-provided text). If any line contains a single quote (`'`), the generated SQL becomes invalid and the migration can fail mid-run. More importantly, interpolating unescaped data into SQL is an injection sink (even if the typical source is an admin setting), and Rails provides `quote(h)`/parameterized inserts to avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3`

`obj[k].map(...)` assumes the value is an array. Any rest-serializer payload with a `*_ids` key that is `null` or a scalar throws `TypeError` and takes down the whole hydrate. Guard with `Ember.isArray`.

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the diff changes the key match from `/(.+)\_id$/` to `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and adds a new branch for plural `*_ids`. In that branch it unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If any payload contains a key ending in `_ids` whose value is `null` (JSON null) or any non-array scalar (string/number/object), this will throw `TypeError: obj[k].map is not a function` and break hydration. This failure mode is directly introduced by the diff because previously `_ids` keys were not matched at all, so there was no `map` call on those values. A guard (e.g., `Ember.isArray(obj[k])`) would prevent the runtime exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `hydrated || []` is dead code — `Array.prototype.map` always returns an array.

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, when handling plural IDs (`m[2]`), the code does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `Array.prototype.map` always returns an Array object (even if empty), `hydrated` will never be falsy, making `|| []` redundant. However, this is not a functional bug introduced by the diff—just an unnecessary fallback (a minor style/cleanup nit).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The branch does `delete obj[k]` **unconditionally**, unlike the singular branch which only deletes when hydration succeeded. Unresolvable ids are silently replaced by `undefined` entries *and* the raw ids are discarded, so callers can't recover. At minimum `.filter(x => x)` the result and keep `obj[k]` when nothing resolved.

adjudication.rationale: In `store._hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` where `m[2]` is truthy) always does `delete obj[k]` after mapping ids via `_lookupSubType`. Unlike the singular branch, it does not check whether hydration succeeded. If `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined`/`null` for some or all ids, the code will still replace the raw `*_ids` array with an array containing unresolved entries and discard the original ids, making recovery impossible. This is a real behavioral inconsistency introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the diff. While the two controller specs added are indeed trivial (they only assert subclassing), the diff also adds substantial model-level coverage in `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` for host normalization (http/https/path trimming) and `host_allowed?`, and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` asserts the embedded topic is created in the embeddable host’s category (i.e., `record_for_host` drives category selection). Therefore it is not true that there is “zero coverage” for these core behaviors, nor is it necessary to “add a spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb” because it already exists. It is true that there’s no request/controller coverage for create/update/destroy or migration backfill, but the proposed finding’s central claim is factually incorrect as stated.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, the `update` action (called by `PUT /admin/customize/embedding`) simply re-renders the serialized embedding from `fetch_embedding` and performs no mutation/persistence at all. This is directly visible in `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb` where `update` has no assignments and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built on each request. On the client, `admin-embedding.js.es6` defines an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but the only template added (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) contains no button or other invocation of `saveChanges`; saving/deleting hosts is handled per-row via the `embeddable-host` component. So the diff introduces (1) an unused client action and (2) a server update endpoint that returns success while saving nothing, which is a concrete correctness/UX defect and misleading API surface.

That is an inconsistency, but the diff shows all current callers handle both safely: `host_allowed?` uses `.present?` (false/nil both => false) and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` (Rails `try` is safe on `false` as well). No correctness bug or security issue is introduced by this mixed return type in the shown code; it’s primarily a consistency/style preference.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A...\Z/i`. In Ruby, `\Z` matches end-of-string *or before a final newline*, so a value like `"example.com\n"` can pass validation and be persisted, since the `before_validation` normalization does not strip whitespace/newlines. That’s a verifiable correctness issue in this added code. Also, the TLD portion `[a-z]{2,5}` will reject valid modern domains with longer TLDs (e.g., `.museum`, `.technology`) and `localhost`, which is a real functional limitation of the added validation.

Even if redundant, this is a minor maintainability/style nit rather than a clear bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff, since repeated filters generally don’t change behavior in a harmful way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`config/routes.rb:153`** — `resources :embeddable_hosts` generates `index`/`show`/`new`/`edit` routes with no corresponding actions. Scope to `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `config/routes.rb` adds `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`, which by default generates the full RESTful set (index/show/new/edit/create/update/destroy). However, the new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy`—there are no `index`, `show`, `new`, or `edit` actions. Those generated routes would therefore route to missing controller actions (typically `AbstractController::ActionNotFound`/404) if requested. Scoping the routes with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` would match the implemented actions and avoid dead routes.
